title: The two-colour Rado number of x - y = z is 5, as a kernel theorem
statement: Every 2-colouring of {1,...,5} contains a monochromatic solution of x = y + z, and some 2-colouring of {1,...,4} avoids one -- the partition {1,4} / {2,3}. So R_2(x-y=z) = 5. This is the two-colour Schur number in Rado form (a = b = 1), and it is the first Rado number in this repository that is a kernel theorem rather than a search certificate: both halves are reconstructed from search into terms `Kernel::add_declaration` accepted, with an empty axiom footprint.

formal.kernel_statement: Nat.Rado.IsRadoNumber a b k n := And (Nat.Rado.Arrows a b k n) (forall m, Nat.lt m n -> Nat.Rado.Arrows a b k m -> False), instantiated at a = b = 1, k = 2, n = 5

evidence.supports: R_2(x-y=z) = 5, both halves, as one kernel term of type Nat.Rado.IsRadoNumber 1 1 2 5
checkers: Kernel::add_declaration (re-derives the type from the proof term)
evidence.notes: `Nat.Rado.schur_arrows_five` (the upper half) is the `Nat.lt_two_cases` decision tree over the 2^5 colour assignments, with the monochromatic triple the search found at each of the 32 leaves; a leaf with no triple makes the builder return `None` and NOTHING is declared. `Nat.Rado.schur_not_arrows_four` (the lower half) refutes `Arrows 1 1 2 4` by reflection against `Nat.Rado.schurSet` = {2,3}: a Bool triple loop over `Nat.Finset.allBelow` that the kernel's own conversion check reduces to `true`, read back at the three existential witnesses by `allBelow_true_at`. The two are joined by `Nat.Rado.isRadoNumber_of_succ` at m = 4. ADR-1596.

evidence.supports: the declaration exists under this exact name and states IsRadoNumber, not something weaker
evidence.checker_command: cargo run --release -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example shape_search -- --name Nat.Rado.schur_two --kind theorem --expect 1
evidence.notes: `shape_search` exits 1 when the count differs and 3 when the query is unanswerable, so a stale index cannot pass for a present declaration.

evidence.supports: 5 is LEAST: the 2^4 subsets of [1,4] contain an avoiding colouring and the 2^5 assignments to [1,5] contain none
evidence.notes: The untrusted half, pinned independently of the kernel term it produced. The `None` at n = 5 is the load-bearing assertion; the test also re-checks the returned set with the witness search and requires that adding the excluded member 1 to it CREATES a monochromatic solution, so a set that merely looked avoiding fails.

provenance.established_by: axeyum lane `rado-in-kernel`, roadmap item W1-1: search in `nat_prelude/rado.rs` produced both certificates and the reconstruction emitted the kernel terms; `Kernel::add_declaration` admitted all 17 declarations on the first attempt
provenance.source: the two-colour Schur number, classical (Schur 1916); a = b = 1 in the Chang-De Loera-Wesley family a(x-y) = bz

prior_art.establishes: S(2) = 4 in the sum-free-partition convention, i.e. R_2(x-y=z) = 5

notes:
`external_status: proved` and `epistemic_status: proved` agree here on purpose: this fact is not a new result, it is the DEMONSTRATION that the computed-to-proved route for a Rado number exists. Its value is the route, not the number.

What it does NOT do is close `F:rado-r4-a5-b3` or `F:rado-r4-a5-b4`, which stay `computed`. ADR-1596 measures why: the statement `Nat.Rado.IsRadoNumber 5 3 4 625` type-checks in this kernel today (unary numerals are FORMED cheaply; the superlinear cost is in reduction, which a Prop mentioning a numeral does not do), so the residue is the proof term, not the numeral. The upper half at 625 would need a term ranging over 4^625 colourings; the lower half at 624 is the reachable frontier at 2.4e8 triples of the same reflection route used here.
